chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Abu Imran Al-Azdi, from Abdullah ibn Al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever says, 'O Lord, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad' one hundred times, one hundred needs will be fulfilled for him: thirty for the world and the remainder for the Hereafter.
ai.seo_question: What are the benefits of reciting Salawat one hundred times according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (as), emphasizing the comprehensive efficacy of Salawat as a means of divine assistance. The specific distribution of thirty worldly needs and seventy for the Hereafter reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that spiritual devotion should not neglect temporal well-being, yet prioritizes eternal success. This hadith underscores the intercessory power of the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt, linking the act of blessing them directly to the resolution of both immediate and ultimate human concerns.
